summary: Converts an axis-angle vector (a2, with the rotation angle encoded as the vector magnitude) into a quaternion written to a1. Writes a1[3] = cos(angle); when sin(angle) is not near zero (FloatRangeCheck), writes a1[0..2] = axis * (sin(angle)/angle); otherwise takes a degenerate near-zero-angle branch. Returns a1.

operations.description: Compute rotation angle v5 as the magnitude of the axis vector a2: v5 = sqrt(a2[0]^2 + a2[1]^2 + a2[2]^2).
Write the quaternion scalar component: a1[3] = cos(v5).
Compute v6 = sin(v5) and hold it for the degenerate check and the scaling factor.
Call FloatRangeCheck(v6, 0.0) to test whether sin(angle) is within range of zero.
Branch on the FloatRangeCheck result: true selects the degenerate near-zero-angle path, false selects the general scaling path.
Degenerate path: copy a1[0..2] from a second pointer (v2). The raw source shows v2 as an uninitialized register-derived value, so the intended copy source is unresolved.
General path: compute the normalization factor v3 = v6 / v5 = sin(angle)/angle.
General path: write a1[0] = v3 * a2[0].
General path: write a1[1] = v3 * a2[1].
General path: write a1[2] = v3 * a2[2].
Return the output quaternion pointer a1.
